brief: JPM's morning briefing leads with today's FOMC: a hike is a done deal, but positioning has turned sharply short into it, so JPM's rates view sees the front end firmer in most scenarios and equities getting relief, with Warsh and the press conference the swing factor. Separately, after AI infra's 'biblical de-rating,' JPM's Gokul argues three questions decide the next leg. Buying compute stays attractive because frontier-model vendors earn 60-80% inference margins and could scale to $20-40bn revenue per GW versus $10bn in 2025. Training will not slow even if new releases face safety limits, since open-source progress and RSI open revenue pools beyond coding. Capex has two more years of room given rising operating cash flow, 13% hyperscaler net debt-to-equity, and equity issuance, with no downturn yet priced into tech hardware. JPM expects leadership to broaden toward inference over training, security software (AI-driven spend could top $430bn across a three-year TAM) and behind-the-meter power (a projected 50-80GW grid shortfall by 2030).
